title: Prakrama 2, Sarga 3. Dispelling the Clouds
html:
The gods come to serve the Lord; He grants boons to His devotees and prema to Shuklambara; Gadadhara's service; the Lord dispels the clouds that hindered the kirtana, while the gods look on from the sky

Verse 1

अथ प्रविष्टो निजवेश्मनि प्रभु-
र्बभौ निशानाथसहस्ररोचिषा।
उवाच चात्रैत्य वसन्ति के जना-
श्चतुर्मुखः षण्मुखपञ्चवक्त्रिणः॥१॥

atha praviṣṭo nijaveśmani prabhu-
rbabhau niśānāthasahasrarociṣā|
uvāca cātraitya vasanti ke janā-
ścaturmukhaḥ ṣaṇmukhapañcavaktriṇaḥ||1||

atha — then; pravishtah — having entered; nija-veshmani — His own house; prabhuh — the Lord; babhau — shone; nisha-natha-sahasra-rochisha — with the light of a thousand moons; uvacha — said; cha — and; atra — here; etya — having come; vasanti — are staying; ke — who; janah — beings; chatur-mukhah — four-faced; shan-mukha-pancha-vaktrinah — six-faced and five-faced.

1Then the Lord entered His house and shone with the light of a thousand moons. And He said: "Who are these beings who have come and are staying here — the four-faced one, the six-faced and the five-faced?1"

Verse 2

श्रीवासनामा द्विजवर्यसत्तमः
श्रुत्वावदत्तं विबुधाः समागताः।
ब्रह्मेश्वरौ षड्वदनादयः प्रभो
त्वां सेवितुं प्रेमरसामृताब्धिम्॥२॥

śrīvāsanāmā dvijavaryasattamaḥ
śrutvāvadattaṁ vibudhāḥ samāgatāḥ|
brahmeśvarau ṣaḍvadanādayaḥ prabho
tvāṁ sevituṁ premarasāmṛtābdhim||2||

shrivasa-nama — named Srivasa; dvija-varya-sattamah — the best of the best brahmanas; shrutva — having heard; avadat — said; tam — to Him; vibudhah — the gods; samagatah — have come; brahma-ishvarau — Brahma and Ishvara (Shiva); shad-vadana-adayah — the Six-faced and others; prabho — O Lord; tvam — You; sevitum — to serve; prema-rasa-amrita-abdhim — the ocean of the nectar of the rasa of love.

2Hearing this, the best of the best brahmanas, named Srivasa, said to Him: "The gods have come — Brahma and Shiva, the Six-faced one and others — O Lord, to serve You, the ocean of the nectar of the rasa of love."

Verse 3

ततः परदिने प्राप्ते शुद्धदेवो वरासने।
उपविश्य स्वभक्तस्य गात्रे पद्भ्यां समस्पृशत्॥३॥

tataḥ paradine prāpte śuddhadevo varāsane|
upaviśya svabhaktasya gātre padbhyāṁ samaspṛśat||3||

tatah — then; para-dine prapte — when the next day came; shuddha-devah — the pure Lord; vara-asane — on an excellent seat; upavishya — seated; sva-bhaktasya — of His devotees; gatre — the bodies; padbhyam — with His feet; samasprishat — touched.

3The next day the pure Lord sat on an exalted seat and touched the bodies of His devotees with His feet.

Verse 4

श्रीवासपण्डिताद्यास्ते प्रणम्य शिरसा हरिम्।
वव्रुस्तच्चरणे भक्तिं प्रेमरूपां सुदुर्लभाम्॥४॥

śrīvāsapaṇḍitādyāste praṇamya śirasā harim|
vavrustaccaraṇe bhaktiṁ premarūpāṁ sudurlabhām||4||

shrivasa-pandita-adyah — Srivasa Pandita and the others; te — they; pranamya — having bowed; shirasa — with their heads; harim — to Hari; vavruh — chose (asked for); tat-charane — for His feet; bhaktim — devotion; prema-rupam — in the form of love; sudurlabham — most rare.

4Srivasa Pandita and the others, bowing their heads to Hari, asked for devotion to His feet — devotion in the form of love, so very rare.

Verse 5

ददौ तेभ्यो वरान्देवो यथेष्टान्भक्तवत्सलः।
शुक्लाम्बरब्रह्मचारी तमूचे पुरुषर्षभम्॥५॥

dadau tebhyo varāndevo yatheṣṭānbhaktavatsalaḥ|
śuklāmbarabrahmacārī tamūce puruṣarṣabham||5||

dadau — gave; tebhyah — to them; varan — boons; devah — the Lord; yatha-ishtan — as they wished; bhakta-vatsalah — loving to His devotees; shuklambara-brahmachari — Shuklambara Brahmachari; tam — to Him; uche — said; purusha-rishabham — the bull among men.

5The Lord, loving to His devotees, granted them the boons they desired. Then Shuklambara Brahmachari said to Him, the bull among men:

Verse 6

भगवन्मथुरां द्वारावतीं गत्वातिदुःखितम्।
मां ज्ञात्वा देहि मे प्रेमभक्तिं तं प्राह स प्रभुः॥६॥

bhagavanmathurāṁ dvārāvatīṁ gatvātiduḥkhitam|
māṁ jñātvā dehi me premabhaktiṁ taṁ prāha sa prabhuḥ||6||

bhagavan — O Bhagavan; mathuram — to Mathura; dvaravatim — to Dvaravati; gatva — having gone; ati-duhkhitam — very unhappy; mam — me; jnatva — knowing; dehi — give; me — to me; prema-bhaktim — loving devotion; tam — to him; praha — said; sah — that; prabhuh — Lord.

6"O Bhagavan, I have been to Mathura and to Dvaravati, and still I am very unhappy. Knowing this, give me loving devotion." The Lord answered him:

Verse 7

जम्बुकाः किं न गच्छन्ति तत्र किं तेन मे भवेत्।
तच्छ्रुत्वैवापतद्भूमौ तमुवाच जनार्दनः॥७॥

jambukāḥ kiṁ na gacchanti tatra kiṁ tena me bhavet|
tacchrutvaivāpatadbhūmau tamuvāca janārdanaḥ||7||

jambukah — jackals; kim na — do not; gachchhanti — go; tatra — there; kim — what; tena — by that; me — to Me; bhavet — would be; tat — that; shrutva eva — just on hearing; apatat — he fell; bhumau — to the ground; tam — to him; uvacha — said; janardanah — Janardana.

7"Do not jackals go there too? What is that to Me?"2 On hearing this he fell to the ground, and Janardana said to him:

Verse 8

भवत्वद्यैव ते प्रेमा तदा तत्क्षणमेव हि।
रुरोद चरणे विष्णोर्निपत्य प्रेमविह्वलः॥८॥

bhavatvadyaiva te premā tadā tatkṣaṇameva hi|
ruroda caraṇe viṣṇornipatya premavihvalaḥ||8||

bhavatu — let there be; adya eva — this very day; te — for you; prema — love; tada — then; tat-kshanam eva hi — at that very moment; ruroda — wept; charane — at the feet; vishnoh — of Vishnu; nipatya — having fallen; prema-vihvalah — overwhelmed by love.

8"Let there be love in you this very day!" — and at that very moment, overwhelmed by love, he fell at the feet of Vishnu and wept.

Verse 9

ततस्ते हृष्टमनसस्तेन सार्धं मुदान्विताः।
जगुः कृष्णस्य गीतानि नामानि च मुहुर्मुहुः॥९॥

tataste hṛṣṭamanasastena sārdhaṁ mudānvitāḥ|
jaguḥ kṛṣṇasya gītāni nāmāni ca muhurmuhuḥ||9||

tatah — then; te — they; hrishta-manasah — with exultant hearts; tena sardham — together with Him; muda-anvitah — joyful; jaguh — sang; krishnasya — of Krishna; gitani — songs; namani — names; cha — and; muhur muhuh — again and again.

9Then all of them, exultant at heart, joyfully sang with Him songs of Krishna, and His names again and again.

Verse 10

गदाधरो महाप्राज्ञो ब्राह्मणः सत्कुलोद्भवः।
प्रेमभक्तश्च तत्पादसन्निकर्षेऽभितिष्ठति॥१०॥

gadādharo mahāprājño brāhmaṇaḥ satkulodbhavaḥ|
premabhaktaśca tatpādasannikarṣe'bhitiṣṭhati||10||

gadadharah — Gadadhara; maha-prajnah — very wise; brahmanah — a brahmana; sat-kula-udbhavah — born of a noble family; prema-bhaktah — a loving devotee; cha — and; tat-pada-sannikarshe — near His feet; abhitishthati — remains.

10The very wise Gadadhara, a brahmana of noble family and a loving devotee, always stayed near His feet.

Verse 11

तेन सार्धं रजन्यां स तिष्ठन्नूचे शुभाक्षरम्।
दातव्यं भवता प्रातर्वैष्णवेभ्यः प्रसादकम्॥११॥

tena sārdhaṁ rajanyāṁ sa tiṣṭhannūce śubhākṣaram|
dātavyaṁ bhavatā prātarvaiṣṇavebhyaḥ prasādakam||11||

tena sardham — with him; rajanyam — at night; sah — He; tishthan — staying; uche — spoke; shubha-aksharam — auspicious words; datavyam — should be given; bhavata — by you; pratah — in the morning; vaishnavebhyah — to the Vaishnavas; prasadakam — (My) prasada.

11One night, while with him, the Lord spoke auspicious words: "In the morning you will give My prasada to the Vaishnavas."

Verse 12

इत्युक्त्वा गात्रमाल्यानि ददौ तस्य करे हरिः।
ततः प्रभाते विमले ते सर्वे समुपागताः॥१२॥

ityuktvā gātramālyāni dadau tasya kare hariḥ|
tataḥ prabhāte vimale te sarve samupāgatāḥ||12||

iti — thus; uktva — having said; gatra-malyani — the garlands from His body; dadau — gave; tasya — his; kare — into the hand; harih — Hari; tatah — then; prabhate — at dawn; vimale — clear; te sarve — they all; samupagatah — assembled.

12Having said this, Hari placed in his hand the garlands from His body. Then, at the clear dawn, they all assembled,

Verse 13

यस्मै यस्मै च यद्दत्तं तत्तस्मै सम्प्रदत्तवान्।
ततस्ते हृष्टमनसः स्नात्वा सुरनदीजले॥१३॥

yasmai yasmai ca yaddattaṁ tattasmai sampradattavān|
tataste hṛṣṭamanasaḥ snātvā suranadījale||13||

yasmai yasmai — to whomever; cha — and; yat — what; dattam — was assigned; tat — that; tasmai — to him; sampradattavan — he handed; tatah — then; te — they; hrishta-manasah — joyful; snatva — having bathed; sura-nadi-jale — in the water of the river of the gods.

13and he handed to each what had been assigned to him. Then, joyful, they bathed in the waters of the river of the gods3,

Verse 14

पूजयित्वा जगन्नाथं नैवेद्यं विनियुज्य च।
पुनस्तं देवदेवेशमाजग्मुर्मुदिताशयाः॥१४॥

pūjayitvā jagannāthaṁ naivedyaṁ viniyujya ca|
punastaṁ devadeveśamājagmurmuditāśayāḥ||14||

pujayitva — having worshipped; jagannatham — the Lord of the world; naivedyam — the food offering; viniyujya — having offered; cha — and; punah — again; tam — to that; deva-deva-isham — Lord of the God of gods; ajagmuh — came; mudita-ashayah — with joyful hearts.

14worshipped the Lord of the world, offered Him food, and with glad hearts came again to Him — the Lord of the God of gods.

Verse 15

गदाधरः प्रत्यहं तं चन्दनेनानुलेपनम्।
कृत्वा माल्यादि गात्रेषु ददाति सततं मुदा॥१५॥

gadādharaḥ pratyahaṁ taṁ candanenānulepanam|
kṛtvā mālyādi gātreṣu dadāti satataṁ mudā||15||

gadadharah — Gadadhara; pratyaham — every day; tam — Him; chandanena — with sandal; anulepanam — anointing; kritva — having done; malya-adi — garlands and so on; gatreshu — on the limbs; dadati — places; satatam — constantly; muda — with joy.

15Every day Gadadhara joyfully anointed Him with sandal paste and constantly adorned His body with garlands and other things.

Verse 16

शयनीये गृहे शय्यां कृत्वा तत्सन्निधौ सुखम्।
स्वपिति श्रद्धया युक्तं शृणु तस्यामृतं वचः॥१६॥

śayanīye gṛhe śayyāṁ kṛtvā tatsannidhau sukham|
svapiti śraddhayā yuktaṁ śṛṇu tasyāmṛtaṁ vacaḥ||16||

shayaniye grihe — in the bedchamber; shayyam — a bed; kritva — having made; tat-sannidhau — near Him; sukham — happily; svapiti — sleeps; shraddhaya yuktam — with faith; shrinu — hear; tasya — about him; amritam — nectarean; vachah — the word.

16In the bedchamber he made a bed for Him and slept happily near Him. Hear with faith the nectarean word about him:

Verse 17

यथा क्वचिद्व्रजे रत्नमन्दिरे कृष्णसन्निधौ।
शय्यां विधाय श्रीराधा स्वपिति प्रेमसंप्लुता॥१७॥

yathā kvacidvraje ratnamandire kṛṣṇasannidhau|
śayyāṁ vidhāya śrīrādhā svapiti premasaṁplutā||17||

yatha — as; kvachit — at times; vraje — in Vraja; ratna-mandire — in a jewelled chamber; krishna-sannidhau — near Krishna; shayyam — a bed; vidhaya — having made; shri-radha — Sri Radha; svapiti — sleeps; prema-sampluta — immersed in love.

17so at times in Vraja, in a jewelled chamber, Sri Radha, having made the bed, sleeps near Krishna, immersed in love4.

Verse 18

सायाह्ने मुदितो देवस्तैः सार्धं कीर्तनोत्सुकः॥१८॥

sāyāhne mudito devastaiḥ sārdhaṁ kīrtanotsukaḥ||18||

sayahne — in the evening; muditah — joyful; devah — the Lord; taih sardham — together with them; kirtana-utsukah — eager for kirtana.

18In the evening the joyful Lord, eager for kirtana, (sang) together with them.

Verse 19

तेऽपि संकीर्तनानन्दमत्ताश्च ननृतुर्जगुः।
श्रीमद्विश्वम्भरेणापि परमानन्दनिर्वृताः॥१९॥

te'pi saṁkīrtanānandamattāśca nanṛturjaguḥ|
śrīmadviśvambhareṇāpi paramānandanirvṛtāḥ||19||

te api — they too; sankirtana-ananda-mattah — intoxicated with the bliss of sankirtana; cha — and; nanrituh — danced; jaguh — sang; shrimad-vishvambharena — with Sriman Vishvambhara; api — also; parama-ananda-nirvritah — enraptured with supreme bliss.

19And they, intoxicated with the bliss of sankirtana, danced and sang together with Sriman Vishvambhara, enraptured with supreme bliss.

Verse 20

कदाचिदावृते व्योम्नि घनैर्गम्भीरनिस्वनैः।
विद्योतिते ततस्तावत्साकं च स्तनयित्नुभिः॥२०॥

kadācidāvṛte vyomni ghanairgambhīranisvanaiḥ|
vidyotite tatastāvatsākaṁ ca stanayitnubhiḥ||20||

kadachit — once; avrite — when covered; vyomni — the sky; ghanaih — by clouds; gambhira-nisvanaih — with deep rumbling; vidyotite — lit by lightning; tatah — then; tavat — at once; sakam — together; cha — and; stanayitnubhih — with thunderclaps.

20Once the sky was covered with deeply rumbling clouds, lit by lightning, and at once the thunder pealed.

Verse 21

वैष्णवा दुःखिताः सर्वे विघ्नोऽयं समुपस्थितः।
मेघा हरेः कीर्तनकेऽभवंश्चिन्तापरा इति॥२१॥

vaiṣṇavā duḥkhitāḥ sarve vighno'yaṁ samupasthitaḥ|
meghā hareḥ kīrtanake'bhavaṁścintāparā iti||21||

vaishnavah — the Vaishnavas; duhkhitah — saddened; sarve — all; vighnah — obstacle; ayam — this; samupasthitah — has arisen; meghah — clouds; hareh — of Hari; kirtanake — at the kirtana; abhavan — became; chinta-parah — absorbed in anxiety; iti — thus (thinking).

21All the Vaishnavas were saddened: "An obstacle has arisen — clouds over Hari's kirtana," and they were filled with anxiety.

Verse 22

तदा तस्मिन्समायातो गृहीत्वा मन्दिरां हरिः।
सुरान्कृतार्थयन्कृष्णं जगौ स स्वजनैः सह॥२२॥

tadā tasminsamāyāto gṛhītvā mandirāṁ hariḥ|
surānkṛtārthayankṛṣṇaṁ jagau sa svajanaiḥ saha||22||

tada — then; tasmin — there; samayatah — having come; grihitva — taking; mandiram — the mandira (small cymbals); harih — Hari; suran — the gods; kritarthayan — fulfilling; krishnam — Krishna; jagau — sang of; sah — He; sva-janaih saha — with His own people.

22Then Hari came there; taking up the mandira5, He sang of Krishna together with His own people, fulfilling the desires of the gods.

Verse 23

ततो मरुद्भिर्मेघौघाः खण्डितास्ते दिगन्तरम्।
भेजुर्बभूव विमलं नभश्चन्द्रांशुरञ्जितम्॥२३॥

tato marudbhirmeghaughāḥ khaṇḍitāste digantaram|
bhejurbabhūva vimalaṁ nabhaścandrāṁśurañjitam||23||

tatah — then; marudbhih — by the winds; megha-aughah — masses of cloud; khanditah — torn apart; te — those; dig-antaram — to the ends of the horizon; bhejuh — went; babhuva — became; vimalam — clear; nabhah — the sky; chandra-amshu-ranjitam — tinted by moonbeams.

23And the winds tore the masses of cloud apart and drove them to the ends of the horizon, and the sky became clear and tinted with moonbeams.

Verse 24

ततः संकीर्तनपरैः साधुभिः सह स प्रभुः।
ननर्त पादकटकै रणच्चरणपङ्कजः॥२४॥

tataḥ saṁkīrtanaparaiḥ sādhubhiḥ saha sa prabhuḥ|
nanarta pādakaṭakai raṇaccaraṇapaṅkajaḥ||24||

tatah — then; sankirtana-paraih — devoted to sankirtana; sadhubhih saha — with the saints; sah — that; prabhuh — Lord; nanarta — danced; pada-katakaih — with anklets; ranat-charana-pankajah — His lotus feet jingling.

24Then, with the saints devoted to sankirtana, the Lord danced, the anklets jingling on His lotus feet.

Verse 25

विप्रसाध्वीमुखाम्भोजघनध्वनिनिनादिते।
नन्दयत्यतिपुष्पौघगन्धोन्मादितदिङ्मुखे॥२५॥

viprasādhvīmukhāmbhojaghanadhvanininādite|
nandayatyatipuṣpaughagandhonmāditadiṅmukhe||25||

vipra-sadhvi-mukha-ambhoja-ghana-dhvani-ninadite — (when all) resounded with the dense sound from the lotus mouths of the saintly brahmana wives; nandayati — delighting; ati-pushpa-augha-gandha-unmadita-din-mukhe — (when) the quarters were intoxicated with the fragrance of abundant flowers.

25All resounded with the dense sound from the lotus mouths of the saintly brahmana wives6; the quarters, to the delight of all, were intoxicated by the fragrance of abundant flowers;

Verse 26

खेऽवस्थिते सुरगणे बभूव महदुत्सवः।
श्रीकृष्णकीर्तनानन्दः सर्वश्रुतिमनोहरः॥२६॥

khe'vasthite suragaṇe babhūva mahadutsavaḥ|
śrīkṛṣṇakīrtanānandaḥ sarvaśrutimanoharaḥ||26||

khe — in the sky; avasthite — stationed; sura-gane — the host of gods; babhuva — there was; mahat — a great; utsavah — festival; shri-krishna-kirtana-anandah — the bliss of Sri Krishna's kirtana; sarva-shruti-manoharah — enchanting to every ear.

26and in the sky stood the host of the gods — and there was a great festival: the bliss of Sri Krishna's kirtana, enchanting to every ear.

Verse 27

येऽनेकजन्मकृतपुण्यसमुद्रसंख्या-
स्ते कृष्णदेवसममेव नितान्तशान्ताः।
नृत्यन्ति हर्षपुलकाश्रुभिरावृताङ्गा
देवा यथाचलभिदा सुखिनो दिविष्ठाः॥२७॥

ye'nekajanmakṛtapuṇyasamudrasaṁkhyā-
ste kṛṣṇadevasamameva nitāntaśāntāḥ|
nṛtyanti harṣapulakāśrubhirāvṛtāṅgā
devā yathācalabhidā sukhino diviṣṭhāḥ||27||

ye — those who; aneka-janma-krita-punya-samudra-sankhyah — whose merits, done in many births, are countless as the ocean; te — they; krishna-deva-samam eva — together with Lord Krishna; nitanta-shantah — utterly at peace; nrityanti — dance; harsha-pulaka-ashrubhih — with thrills of joy and tears; avritangah — their limbs covered; devah — the gods; yatha — as; achala-bhida — with the Splitter of mountains (Indra); sukhinah — happy; divishthah — dwelling in heaven.

27Those whose merits, earned over many births, are countless as the waters of the ocean, now utterly at peace, dance together with Lord Krishna, covered with thrills of joy and tears, like the happy gods in heaven with the Splitter of mountains7.

Thus ends the third sarga, "Dispelling the Clouds" (Megha-nivarana), of the second prakrama of the great poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. The four-faced one is Brahma; the six-faced is Skanda (Karttikeya), Shiva's son; the five-faced is Shiva.
  2. The Lord does not belittle the holy places: He means that merely being bodily present in Mathura and Dvaravati, without love, does not yet bear fruit — jackals, after all, roam there too. Shuklambara was asking precisely for love, and the Lord granted it at once (v. 8).
  3. The river of the gods is the Ganga.
  4. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition, Gadadhara Pandita is Sri Radha Herself appearing in Gauranga's lila (Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika 147); that is why Murari compares his service with Radha's. Both are pure prema, without a trace of the mundane.
  5. The mandira is a pair of small brass cymbals that keep the rhythm in kirtana.
  6. That is, the auspicious "ulu-ulu" sound with which Bengali women greet a festive occasion.
  7. The Splitter of mountains is Indra, king of the gods.
